title: Traffic mirroring: sampled duplication, safe isolation, and cost-aware throttling
creator: Maya Patel
description: Implement a production-grade traffic mirroring pipeline that safely duplicates a deterministic sample of live requests into an isolated shadow path for model evaluation. The feature must: (1) support deterministic sampling by user/customer/route, (2) ensure PII-safe scrubbing and storage TTL, (3) execute mirrored inference on isolated compute (sandbox cluster or quantized variant) with resource accounting, and (4) provide runtime cost throttles and auto-disable triggers integrated with rollout automation.
acceptance_criteria: Config knob to enable mirroring per route with a stable sample fraction and deterministic hashing (by user id or request id)
Mirrored traffic is tagged and routed to a sandbox inference pool with separate billing and no impact to primary latency SLOs
PII scrubber runs inline before duplication; mirrored request bodies are stored encrypted with configurable TTL (default 7 days)
Cost controller enforces budget-driven throttle: per-hour token cap and burn-rate based scaling back of mirror fraction
Telemetry shows message-level correlation between original and mirrored responses; dashboard displays divergence metrics and cost consumed

Auto-disable policy that flips mirroring off when: token burn > budget, mirrored error-rate delta > 2.0%, end-to-end latency increase on primary > 5% attributed to mirroring proxy (should be 0 in our design)
E2E test harness that replays 1M requests at peak QPS to verify isolation, sampling correctness, and budget enforcement
design_considerations: Deterministic sampling: use consistent hashing with salt per-deployment to ensure stable populations across restarts
Isolation model: prefer separate Kubernetes/GPU node pool + admission controller to prevent noisy neighbor effects; fallback to resource-limited containers running quantized models for lower cost
Scrubbing: implement rule-based stripping of known PII keys and token-level mask using existing redact library; mark un-scrubbable records for truncation only
Cost accounting: attribute token counts for mirrored calls to a shadow billing ledger linked to the owning project; allow manual budget top-ups

Latency posture: mirroring must be async and non-blocking for the primary request path (sidecar or gateway duplication). Any sync mirroring attempts must be behind an opt-in flag and limited to internal canaries
Observability: link mirrored requests to the primary via correlation IDs and surface aggregated divergence (BLEU/embedding cosine/LLR) where applicable
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (API+Gateway): Add mirror header propagation and deterministic sampler in API gateway; basic sidecar duplication to Kafka topic
Phase 2 (Worker + Sandbox): Consume mirror topic from workers, apply scrubbing, write to encrypted storage, and forward to sandbox inference cluster
Phase 3 (Cost controls + Dashboard): Implement budget enforcement service and dashboard hooks; add rollback triggers into rollout controller
Phase 4 (Policies + Tests): Integrate with rollout automation for auto-disable and A/B variant comparison; run large-scale replay tests and a staged rollout to internal teams
Phase 5 (Hardening): Security review, SOC compliance checks, and on-call runbook for mirror-induced incidents
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Mirroring increases overall token spend unexpectedly. Mitigation: hard budget guardrails and token caps on mirror pool; alerting when 70% of budget used
Risk: Mirrored data contains PII. Mitigation: mandatory scrubbing step before persistence and access controls on mirror store; security review required
Risk: Sandbox compute saturates and affects other workloads. Mitigation: enforce node taints/quotas and autoscale limits; use lower-cost quantized models for mirror path
Risk: Sampling bias yields unrepresentative evaluation. Mitigation: support stratified sampling (by geography, user-tier, route) and randomized A/B complement runs
